newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis down, supply looms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis down, supply looms.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended down 1/4 to 1/2 point and more in spots as March jobs data bruised U.S. Treasuries and munis braced for what is expected to be the year's biggest new issue week so far at $4.5 billion.
One trader said while the broader municipal market ended down 1/2, long New York City bonds took a bigger hit, ending down 3/4 of a point.
"A lot of the New York names got hammered," the trader said. "There's a lot of paper coming so they probably took a disproportionate hit today than some of the other sectors.
A $900 million New York City general obligation bond offering is set for Wednesday via lead underwriter Smith Barney Inc.

The city Friday began its retail order period, setting the top yield in 2027 at 6.35 percent. By late Friday, $134 million of retail orders had been received. The order period ends Tuesday at noon EDT.

Other negotiated deals expected next week include $260.7 million Puerto Rico Municipal Finance Agency deal via Morgan Stanley & Co and a $231 million Delaware County Industrial Development Authority, Pa., offering through Goldman Sachs & Co.
On the competitive side, Tuesday is the big day with a $307 million Georgia deal is set for 1100 EDT and a $300 million Clark County School District, Nevada offering is scheduled for 1130 EDT.
A trader observed that, until now, municipal volume has been relatively light, which has allowed the market to become rich to Treasuries.
"That could change," he said. "The calendar is pretty big, and it's not like there is a ton of money flowing into the market, even at adjusted levels."
While long munis are hovering right around the magic six percent level, "it's still not that easy to get six percent in the long end of the market," the trader said.
"Guys are reluctant to sell anything at a six percent," he said.
A municipal analyst warned that next week's new issues could usher in a "radical change down" for the market.
"I don't think people have been willing to feel the pain quite yet in here," he said, adding "It might be a rude shock by Tuesday."

As for Friday's secondary market action, the analyst said high-grade issues worsened by about three basis points, while dollar bonds ended down 3/8 of a point to more in spots. Overall, muni cash ended down about 1/4 to 3/8 of point, he said.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed down 18/32 at 111-23/32. The June T-bond contract closed down 20/32 at 107. The MOB spread was 151 ticks.
In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed off its lows but down 20/32 at 93-28/32 to yield 7.12 percent.
Bonds took a hit after the release of the March jobs figures even though the headline number printed below expectations.

The U.S. Labor Department said the economy added 175,000 new jobs in March, and the jobless rate fell to 5.2 percent. Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast 196,000 new jobs and a 5.2 percent unemployment rate.

But market analysts said the figures showed enough strength to increase the likelihood of another interest-rate hike. Traders cited the increase in average hourly earnings to $12.15 in March from $12.10 in February as a concern.
((--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655))
